test_title: PYST 38: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 14 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A metallic conductor obeys Ohm’s law at room temperature. When the applied potential difference across it is increased from V to 2V, and the temperature is kept constant, the current through the conductor:

options.text: Remains unchanged because current depends only on resistance
More than doubles due to increased electron drift velocity
Less than doubles due to heating effects

solution:
The correct answer is __**Doubles because resistance is constant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ohm’s Law** states that the current (**I**) flowing through a metallic conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference (**V**) applied across its ends, provided its physical conditions such as **temperature** remain constant.
 
• The mathematical expression for this relationship is **V = I * R**, where **R** represents the **Electrical Resistance** of the conductor.
 
• In this scenario, since the **temperature is kept constant**, the resistance (**R**) of the metallic conductor remains unchanged regardless of the change in voltage.
 
• When the potential difference is increased from **V** to **2V**, the new current (**I'**) can be calculated using the formula **I' = (2V) / R**. Since **I = V / R**, it follows that **I' = 2 * I**.
 
• The current **doubles** because it maintains a **linear relationship** with the potential difference in an ohmic conductor. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Statement 1 is incorrect because while current does depend on resistance, it is also a function of the applied **potential difference**.
 
• Statement 3 is incorrect because at a constant temperature, the **drift velocity** of electrons increases proportionally with the electric field (and thus voltage), leading exactly to a doubling of current, not "more than double."
 
• Statement 4 is incorrect because the question explicitly specifies that the **temperature is kept constant**, which implies any **heating effects** (Joule heating) are either neglected or compensated for to keep **R** stable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electrical Resistance (R):** It is the property of a material to oppose the flow of **electric current**. The **SI unit** of resistance is the **Ohm** (represented by the Greek letter **Ω**).
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance:** The resistance of a conductor depends on its **length** (directly proportional), **area of cross-section** (inversely proportional), the **nature of the material** (resistivity), and **temperature**.
 
• **Drift Velocity:** This is the average velocity attained by **charged particles** (such as electrons) in a material due to an **electric field**. The current (**I**) is defined as **I = n * A * e * Vd**, where **Vd** is the drift velocity. Since **Vd** is proportional to **V**, current is also proportional to **V**.
 
• **Ohmic and Non-Ohmic Devices:**
 
 
• **Ohmic Conductors:** Materials like **Copper**, **Silver**, and **Aluminum** that follow Ohm's law, showing a straight-line **V-I graph** passing through the origin.
 
• **Non-Ohmic Conductors:** Devices like **semiconductors**, **diodes**, and **transistors** where the resistance changes as the voltage or current changes, resulting in a non-linear **V-I characteristic**.
 
 
 
• **Temperature Coefficient:** For pure metals, resistance increases with an increase in **temperature**. This is because the thermal vibrations of metal ions increase, leading to more frequent collisions with **drifting electrons**. However, in this specific problem, the constant temperature constraint ensures **Ohm's Law** is strictly followed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ohm's Law Discovery:** The law was named after the German physicist **Georg Simon Ohm**, who published his findings in **1827**.
 
• **Power Dissipation:** When current flows through a resistor, electrical energy is converted into heat. This is known as **Joule Heating**, given by **P = I² * R** or **P = V² / R**. In real-world applications, if the voltage doubles, the power dissipation increases **four times**, which would normally raise the temperature unless cooled.
 
• **Conductance:** The reciprocal of resistance is called **conductance (G)**, measured in **Siemens (S)** or **mho**. **G = 1 / R**.
